artifacts.synopsis: TE David Kniseley and others challenged Rocky Mountain Presbytery's approval of the public title “Minister of Church Life” for an unordained female staff member. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that “minister” has a specific technical meaning in the BCO but that the BCO is silent on generic titles for non-ordained staff, leaving that use to lower-court judgment subject to BCO 40-2(3); a dissent disagreed.

artifacts.title: Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Mrs. Plowman was suspended from the Lord's Table and found guilty of contumacy by the Session of Lehigh Valley Presbyterian Church after refusing to compel her minor daughters to testify; her subsequent appeal was informally rejected by the chairman of Presbytery's Judicial Business Committee, who advised her to refile as a complaint. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that Mrs. Plowman had submitted to regular trial and had a right to appeal, and remanded the case to Philadelphia Presbytery for adjudication.

artifacts.synopsis: Central Carolina Presbytery remanded complaints to an Interim Session Commission rather than adjudicating them directly. The SJC confirmed this action, finding that the Commission appointed as Interim Session was the proper court of original jurisdiction and remanding the complaints for adjudication by that Commission.
